thread:
sarah: Heads-up — seeing a sustained drop in prompt/prefix cache hit-rate for redwood-3b-quant on /generate over the last 12h (global 71% -> 63%). Noticed token-saved also down by ~20%.

raj: Same trend on /chat in us-west-2. Top-customer slice (cust_042) accounts for ~40% of the delta.

metrics-bot: ALERT: cache_hit_rate(redwood-3b-quant, /generate) decreased from 0.71 to 0.63 over 12h. token_saved_24h decreased 1.2M -> 970k. Triggered anomaly rule: slice_drop > 10%.

matt: Dumped a few sample cache keys from requests hitting cust_042 — lots of variation in trailing punctuation and newline chars. Example key format we use now: `cache_key = f"{model}:{route}:{prompt_hash}:{customer_id}"`
Potential culprit: prompt normalization changed in a small refactor last week, preserving trailing whitespace.

olivia: I can roll a canary that normalizes whitespace + collapses repeated "\n" and strips trailing punctuation in the keying layer. Pushing patch to canary now.

sarah: Can we add panels that show hit-rate by (model, route, customer) and token-saved per-customer? Also want a metric for key_entropy so we can detect high-variance keying.

kevin: I will add a Grafana dashboard tile for top-k customer token-saved and a panel for key_entropy (Shannon). For alerts: propose alert when top10 token-saved drops >10% vs 7d median.

raj: Also flagging yesterday's runtime kernel change — did we change kernel selection heuristics around 03:20 UTC? If kernel changes increased avg prefix length or altered KV layout, that could affect warmup behavior.

matt: Profiled a few hot hosts — KV lookup p95 unchanged (0.9ms). Misses correlate with key mismatch, not latency. Batching heuristics did change earlier but only to allow larger batch windows for >2s tails; unlikely to cause systematic missing.

olivia: For retrospective analysis, we can recompute request-level hit/miss and token-saved from request logs. BigQuery snippet I'm using to reconstruct per-request cache outcome:

```
SELECT
  customer_id,
  model,
  route,
  COUNTIF(cache_hit) AS hits,
  COUNTIF(NOT cache_hit) AS misses,
  SUM(tokens_saved) AS tokens_saved
FROM `prod_logs.prefix_cache_events`
WHERE _PARTITIONTIME BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 14 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
GROUP BY customer_id, model, route
ORDER BY tokens_saved DESC
LIMIT 200;
```

matt: Ran that for last 7 days — cust_042 has 18k extra misses vs previous window; keys show high entropy in the prompt_hash segment. Looks like a normalization regression.

sarah: Canary fix applied by olivia rolled to 5% of traffic at 14:10 UTC — hit-rate on the canary group jumped from 64% -> 72% within 45 minutes. Token-saved on canary +9.8%.

kevin: I'll promote the normalization to 50% after a smoke check and add two alert rules: (1) key_entropy increase > 0.5 nats for top50 customers, (2) token_saved drop > 10% sustained 6h.

raj: Long-term we should add a preflight test in CI that computes a small fingerprint of key distribution for a sample prompt set and compares entropy to baseline. That would've caught this during the refactor.

matt: Agreed. Also we should add a lightweight unit that simulates warmup and reports expected hit-rate delta when kernel/kv/layout changes.

olivia: Canary now at 50% and metrics look clean. Rolling to 100% in 10m.

sarah: Thanks all. Postmortem-lite to follow: root cause = prompt normalization refactor that preserved trailing whitespace -> key variance -> hit-rate drop. Mitigation = normalization + new dashboard/alerts. Will create the ops note and link dashboards. :thumbsup:

metrics-bot: Note: dashboard panels created: `cache.hit_rate_by_model_route_customer`, `cache.tokens_saved_per_customer`, `cache.key_entropy_by_customer`. Historical backfill for last 30 days scheduled.

kevin: FYI I'm adding a small panel that correlates `kernel_version` with `avg_prefix_len` and `hit_rate` so future kernel rollouts can be pegged to cache behavior.

matt: Leaving logs of sample bad keys in the incident doc. If anyone needs the extraction query ping me.

sarah: closing loop — no further regression after full rollout. Thanks everyone.
